overview.headline: Unresolved backlog and widespread feature demand (105 requests) are driving negative sentiment (54%) and measurable churn risk (20%).
overview.summary: Across 150 records we see a dominant pattern: 105 feature requests (70% of records) and 140 unresolved issues (93.3%) coincide with more negative than positive sentiment (81 negative, 54.0%). Top topics center on feature requests, support, onboarding and integrations (Salesforce and calendar sync called out in the problem list). Chat is the primary support channel (105 chats), and most reports come from Pro customers and startups. The scale of unresolved items is the clearest operational failure and is amplifying requests and dissatisfaction.
overview.priority: Immediately reduce the unresolved-issue backlog and fast-track the highest-impact feature requests (integrations, reporting, billing/invoice history) by dedicating engineering and support resources to close 140 outstanding issues and ship targeted fixes/integrations.

problems.name: missing_invoice_history
problems.summary: The single biggest recurring problem is unmet core functionality coupled with an unresolved-support backlog: 105 explicit feature requests and specific missing items (Salesforce integration, calendar sync, invoice history, two‑factor authentication, team management panel, approval-workflow gaps) appear repeatedly while 140 of 150 records remain unresolved. That combination creates persistent friction—customers ask for capabilities that aren’t available and then don’t get timely closure from support.

feature_request_insight: Feature demand is concentrated on integrations (Salesforce and calendar sync), better reporting/analytics, billing and invoice history, and admin/team-management controls; these specific gaps are present in the top_problems list and feature_topics. Because 70% of records contain feature requests and integration/reporting appear repeatedly, items framed as capability questions (e.g., “missing_salesforce_integration”) should be treated as explicit requests. Prioritizing these features will address the largest documented demand signals.
churn_insight: There is meaningful retention risk: 30 records (20%) contain churn signals, disproportionately tied to integration, billing, and usability issues (integration:5, billing:4, usability:4 in churn_topics). The very high unresolved-issue rate (140 records) and prevailing negative sentiment suggest customers needing integrations or billing clarity are most likely to leave unless issues are resolved or mitigations (clear timelines, compensations, or hands-on onboarding) are provided.
